# Doctrines & Laws

> Law, explained. A free legal-education initiative of Doctrines & Laws Chambers, New Delhi: plain-language explainers on Indian law for citizens and law students, and free UPSC Civil Services Law Optional study notes. General information only, not legal advice.

## Main sections

- [Home](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/): this week in court, know-your-rights guides, landmark cases, IPC to BNS section finder, official resources
- [Explainers](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/): one judgment or statute per page, answered in plain English
- [UPSC Law Optional](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/upsc-law/): study notes, answer frames and previous-year questions (2013 onwards) for every syllabus unit

## Explainers

- [Seven years in jail after acquittal: what does Article 21 owe you?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/acquittal-compensation/): The Supreme Court awarded ₹30 lakh in public-law compensation and asked Parliament to enact a law on wrongful incarceration.
- [How do I protect my brand name? Trademark basics in India](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/trademark-basics/): File online with IP India for ₹4,500 a class if you are an individual, startup or small business. What registration protects, and what ™ and ® mean.
- [Can an online seller refuse a return or a refund?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/online-returns-refunds/): Not if the product is defective, fake, not as described or delivered late. What the e-commerce rules say, and how to complain if a platform won’t budge.
- [New labour codes: what changed for employees?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/labour-codes/): Four codes replaced 29 labour laws on 21 November 2025. Appointment letters, gratuity after one year for fixed-term staff, and what else to know.
- [How is crypto taxed in India? The 30% rule explained](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/crypto-tax/): Gains on crypto and other virtual digital assets are taxed at a flat 30%, with 1% TDS on sales. What changed under the Income-tax Act, 2025.
- [How many SIM cards can be in your name? Limits and penalties](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/sim-cards-in-your-name/): Nine across India, six in J&K, Assam and the North-East. How to check the numbers issued in your name, and block the ones you don’t use.
- [Is esports legal in India? What the Online Gaming Act says](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/esports-law/): Yes. The Online Gaming Act, 2025 recognises e-sports as competitive sport, separate from banned real-money games. How recognition and registration work.
- [Lost money to an online fraud? What to do in the first hour](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/online-fraud-first-hour/): Call 1930 or report on cybercrime.gov.in at once, then tell your bank. Speed decides whether the money can be frozen before it moves on.
- [Is there such a thing as a “digital arrest”?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/digital-arrest/): No. Indian law has no procedure for arresting anyone over a video call. How the scam works, and what the Supreme Court has ordered.
- [When must a social media platform take down a post?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/platform-takedowns/): Section 79 of the IT Act shields platforms only if they act on lawful orders. Since February 2026 the deadline is three hours, not 36.
- [Your personal data was leaked. What must the company tell you?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/dpdp-data-breach/): Under the DPDP Rules, 2025, a company must tell affected users without delay and report to the Data Protection Board within 72 hours.
- [Deepfakes and AI-made content: what the 2026 IT Rules require](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/deepfake-labelling/): Since 20 February 2026, AI-generated audio, images and video must carry a clear label and embedded provenance data. What platforms and AI tools must do.
- [Can AI companies train on your work? The ANI v. OpenAI ruling](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/ai-training-copyright/): The Delhi High Court refused an interim injunction against ChatGPT, finding training prima facie fair dealing. What it decided and what is still open.
- [Who can use a celebrity’s face or voice? Personality rights](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/personality-rights/): Courts protect a well-known person’s name, image, voice and likeness from commercial misuse, including AI deepfakes, voice clones and chatbots.
- [UA 7+, 13+, 16+: film certification and piracy law explained](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/film-certification/): The 2023 amendment to the Cinematograph Act added age-based ratings, made certificates permanent and made camcording and piracy specific offences.
- [What the National Sports Governance Act, 2025 changes](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/sports-governance-act/): A National Sports Board now recognises federations and a Sports Tribunal hears disputes, with appeals to the Supreme Court.
- [Is real-money online gaming banned in India?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/online-gaming-ban/): Yes. Since 1 May 2026 the Online Gaming Act bans offering, advertising and processing payments for online money games. Players are not punished.
- [Hidden charges at checkout? Dark patterns explained](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/dark-patterns/): Indian law bans 13 “dark patterns” on apps and websites, from fake countdown timers to items sneaked into your cart. What they are and how to complain.
- [Can I file an FIR at any police station? Zero FIR explained](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/zero-fir/): Yes. Under Section 173 of the BNSS, police must record a cognizable offence wherever it happened and transfer it. How to file, and what to do if refused.
- [One dashboard for all your data permissions?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/dpdp-consent-manager/): How Consent Managers under the DPDP Act, 2023 and Rule 4 of the DPDP Rules, 2025 are meant to work.
- [Can a government order rely on case law invented by AI?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/ai-hallucinated-citations/): The Bombay High Court quashed a customs order that cited judgments that do not exist.
- [When does an autonomous body become “State”?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/article-12-nbt/): The Supreme Court held that the National Book Trust is “State” under Article 12.
- [Can the police summon you to “settle” a property dispute?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/police-civil-disputes/): Police investigate crime; civil courts decide property disputes.
- [“Law and order” or “public order”? The concentric circles test](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/public-order/): Why not every crime justifies preventive detention under Article 22.
- [Can a WhatsApp screenshot alone get someone convicted?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/whatsapp-evidence/): Admissibility is one hurdle; proving who wrote the message is another.
- [Road accident? Interim relief without proving fault](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/mv-interim-relief/): Section 164A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 provides for quick interim compensation.
- [Can the State ban a protest just to manage traffic?](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/right-to-protest/): Article 19(1)(b), the public trust doctrine and the proportionality test.

## Explainer topics

- [Cyber law](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/cyber-law/): Online fraud, digital arrest scams, hacking and identity theft: what Indian law says and what to do when it happens to you.
- [Technology](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/technology/): How Indian law regulates platforms, apps and the internet: safe harbour, takedowns, blocking orders and your remedies as a user.
- [AI & law](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/ai-and-law/): Deepfakes, AI-generated content, copyright and AI training, and the rules India has made for artificial intelligence.
- [Data privacy](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/data-privacy/): Your rights over personal data under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the DPDP Rules, 2025.
- [Entertainment & media](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/entertainment-and-media/): Film certification, piracy, personality rights, celebrity deepfakes and the law that governs films, music and streaming.
- [Sports & gaming](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/sports-and-gaming/): Sports governance, athletes' rights, sports disputes, e-sports and the ban on real-money online games.
- [Consumer](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/consumer/): Your rights as a buyer online and offline: dark patterns, hidden charges, refunds and how to complain.
- [IP & trademarks](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/ip-and-trademarks/): Trademarks, copyright and brand protection for creators, startups and small businesses, explained in plain language.
- [Employment](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/employment/): Your rights at work under the four labour codes: wages, gratuity, appointment letters, gig work and how to complain.
- [Tax](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/tax/): Tax questions people actually ask, explained under the Income-tax Act, 2025.
- [Constitutional](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/constitutional/): Fundamental rights, the limits of State power and landmark constitutional judgments, explained in plain language.
- [Criminal](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/criminal/): FIRs, arrest, bail and the new criminal laws (BNS, BNSS and BSA), explained for citizens.
- [Civil](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/civil/): Property disputes, accident compensation and everyday civil law questions.
- [Evidence](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/evidence/): How courts treat electronic records, WhatsApp chats and other evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
- [Administrative](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/explainers/topic/administrative/): How government bodies must act: natural justice, reasoned orders and judicial review.

## UPSC Law Optional subjects

- [Constitutional and Administrative Law](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/upsc-law/constitutional-administrative-law/): Paper I, 16 units
- [International Law](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/upsc-law/international-law/): Paper I, 15 units
- [Law of Crimes](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/upsc-law/law-of-crimes/): Paper II, 12 units
- [Law of Torts](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/upsc-law/law-of-torts/): Paper II, 13 units
- [Law of Contracts and Mercantile Law](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/upsc-law/contracts-mercantile-law/): Paper II, 13 units
- [Contemporary Legal Developments](https://doctrinesandlaws.netlify.app/upsc-law/contemporary-legal-developments/): Paper II, 8 units
